definition_review.statement:
A cross-type mixing and reaction network consists of a declared set $\mathcal G$ of tagged composition types and a state set $X_\Gamma$ for each type. Each state set comes with a fixed formal composition $\nu_\Gamma$, and its states satisfy $\nu(x)=\nu_\Gamma$ as in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. These mathematical coefficients and their positive type weights are distinct from dimensioned material amounts. For physical channels the model additionally supplies endpoint quantity maps $U_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $n_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ in a declared finite species list, together with any separately tracked mechanical or external-field endpoint quantities. No identification of two distinct scaled tags is made.

For each channel $\alpha$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$, the model supplies sets $Z_\alpha$ of configurations, $\mathcal K_\alpha$ of protocol records, $\mathcal B_\alpha$ of outer-boundary records, and $\mathcal R_\alpha$ of transfer records, and equilibrium subsets and endpoint maps $\xi^-_\alpha:Z^-_\alpha\to X_\Gamma$, $\xi^+_\alpha:Z^+_\alpha\to X_{\Gamma'}$. A typed record is
$$P=(I,x^-,x^+,z,\kappa,b,r),$$
where $I=[t_0,t_1]$, $t_0<t_1$, is a finite time interval in seconds, $x^-\in X_\Gamma$, $x^+\in X_{\Gamma'}$, $z:I\to Z_\alpha$, $z(t_0)\in Z^-_\alpha$, $z(t_1)\in Z^+_\alpha$, $\xi^-_\alpha(z(t_0))=x^-$, $\xi^+_\alpha(z(t_1))=x^+$, $\kappa\in\mathcal K_\alpha$, $b\in\mathcal B_\alpha$, and $r\in\mathcal R_\alpha$. Transfer maps $Q_\alpha,W_{\mathrm{on},\alpha}:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $N_\alpha:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ record heat, work and material transfer with declared signs; any tracked $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ are also joule-valued record maps. The channel specifies a balance predicate on this typed record set, or equivalently a balance map into a declared product of quantity spaces whose required value is zero, and a model-admitted subset satisfying that predicate. The predicate states the actual energy and material constraints of that channel; no balance law, physical admission or endpoint realizability follows from the tuple alone. For a fixed-constitution core closed channel, its endpoint embeddings, fields and admitted subset are exactly those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with no material transfer and its stated kinetic/external restrictions. Other channels require their own adopted constraints. Define $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$ exactly when an admitted channel record has those endpoints. No channel is inferred from separated composition.

For any permitted equal-formal-mass compound states $A,B$ of the network, define $A\prec B$ exactly when at least one admitted channel record has initial state $A$ and final state $B$; for named single types this is the relation $\mathcal R$ above. This is the exact relation supplied to [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], not a separate abstract order that enlarges or restricts the channel edges. Its extension to finite tagged products and common spectators is governed by the adopted A1–A6 conditions below. Thus every edge in a decorated chain is precisely an admitted channel transition. This identification is a declared model condition.

The network is **finite-factor closed** when its types admit the declared finite composition and positive scaling operations and each allowed channel respects the model’s stated conservation constraints. In addition, each channel must preserve the dimensionless formal mass $m$ of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]; this is the equal-coefficient-mass convention required by the mathematical chain-cost supplier, not a statement that formal mass is kilograms or moles. The common relation on all equal-formal-mass compounds satisfies A1–A6 of [[post-td-accessibility-a1-a6]], including consistency with spectators and stability. A decorated finite chain is exactly a finite sequence of such allowed transitions with a common catalyst and the real baseline-entropy edge costs in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]].

For $\Gamma,\Gamma'$, let $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$ be the infimum of those finite decorated-chain costs, with $+\infty$ if no witness exists and $-\infty$ if costs are unbounded below. The network has **no sinks** when, for every ordered type pair,

$$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty.$$

No-sinks is an explicit property required of a network used in the global-offset theorem; it is not proved by this definition, and it is not asserted for every physical mixing or reaction. The definition permits the channel set to be empty; then the condition must still be checked rather than inferred.

case_scope.source_excerpt:
Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

Use the dimensionless coordinates, simple configurations, and pair potential of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. A sequence $(\Lambda_k)_{k\geq1}$ of bounded measurable regions is van Hove if $|\Lambda_k|\to\infty$ and, for every fixed $s>0$,
$$\frac{|\{x\in\Lambda_k:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Lambda_k)\leq s\}|}{|\Lambda_k|}\longrightarrow0.$$
This is an explicit condition on the boundary-layer volume; increasing volume alone does not imply it. A free wall permits particles only in $\Lambda_k$ and includes no exterior particles. A periodic wall uses the specified periodic cell and its image convention.

For the deterministic exterior class, let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and $\Lambda_n=[-n-1/2,n+1/2)^d$, with $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$. For a locally finite exterior configuration $\zeta\subset\mathbb R^d$, write $N_{C+i}(\zeta)=|\zeta\cap(C+i)|$. Given $t<\infty$, define
$$\Omega(t)=\left\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C+i}(\zeta)^2\leq tV_n\ \text{for every integer }n\geq0\right\}.$$
For an interior configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_n$, its exterior interaction is
$$W_n(\omega,\zeta)=\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n}\varphi(x-y),$$
interpreted as an extended-real sum. A positive infinite value has zero Boltzmann weight. The regular tail controls distant terms; the class $\Omega(t)$ is a fixed uniform bound on exterior cell counts, not permission for an arbitrary volume-filling external potential. The van Hove and uniformly tempered exterior conditions are separate boundary regimes.

Use the dimensionless coordinates, simple configurations, and pair potential of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. A sequence $(\Lambda_k)_{k\geq1}$ of bounded measurable regions is van Hove if $|\Lambda_k|\to\infty$ and, for every fixed $s>0$,
$$\frac{|\{x\in\Lambda_k:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Lambda_k)\leq s\}|}{|\Lambda_k|}\longrightarrow0.$$
This is an explicit condition on the boundary-layer volume; increasing volume alone does not imply it. A free wall permits particles only in $\Lambda_k$ and includes no exterior particles. A periodic wall uses the specified periodic cell and its image convention.

For the deterministic exterior class, let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and $\Lambda_n=[-n-1/2,n+1/2)^d$, with $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$. For a locally finite exterior configuration $\zeta\subset\mathbb R^d$, write $N_{C+i}(\zeta)=|\zeta\cap(C+i)|$. Given $t<\infty$, define
$$\Omega(t)=\left\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C+i}(\zeta)^2\leq tV_n\ \text{for every integer }n\geq0\right\}.$$
For an interior configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_n$, its exterior interaction is
$$W_n(\omega,\zeta)=\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n}\varphi(x-y),$$
interpreted as an extended-real sum. A positive infinite value has zero Boltzmann weight. The regular tail controls distant terms; the class $\Omega(t)$ is a fixed uniform bound on exterior cell counts, not permission for an arbitrary volume-filling external potential. The van Hove and uniformly tempered exterior conditions are separate boundary regimes.

$$S_n(N_n,e,\delta_n)=\{\omega\subset\Lambda_n:|\omega|=N_n,\ |H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n\}.$$

This is not a surface measure on an exact-energy hypersurface and not a phase-space shell for $K(p)+H_N^{\mathrm{per}}$.

For the pair potential $\varphi$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$. A finite configuration is hard-admissible if every pair displacement avoids $B$. For $z>0$, define the retained-admissibility zero-inverse-temperature free-wall weight of $\omega$ to be
$$w_0(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\{H_{N(\omega)}(\omega)<\infty\}}.$$
Its finite-volume partition sum, when finite, is $\Xi_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ret},0}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_0(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)$, using [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This definition sets the weight of a forbidden configuration to zero; it does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$. When $B=\varnothing$ the measure is the unrestricted Poisson activity model; for a nonempty hard core it is generally not Poisson. The convention is explicit model data and carries no statement about an arbitrary zero-width energy shell.

For a periodic cell of side $L$ in dimensionless coordinates, use the exact image energy $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Its periodic retained-admissibility weight is
$$w_{L,0}^{\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)<+\infty\}}=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{\varphi(y-x)<+\infty\text{ for every }x\in\omega,\ y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x\}}.$$
Thus every forbidden pair between distinct particles and every forbidden periodic-image pair, including a particle with one of its own nontrivial images, receives zero weight. Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.

derivations.claim: By [A1], the physical positional partition sum is $\Xi_L(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda_L,N}$. Set $\alpha=\log z$; then $z^N=e^{\alpha N}$. Translate the centered cube by $L/2$ in each coordinate to $[0,L)^d$; this preserves Lebesgue measure and every pair displacement, so the positional partition is exactly the free-cube sum of [L1]. The dimensionless energy conversion in [F1] matches its numerical $\widehat\beta$.

The conditional conclusion of [L1] gives a finite limit $P(\log z,\widehat\beta)$ for $|\Lambda_L|^{-1}\log\Xi_L$. Multiplying by $k_BT/\ell_0^d$, which is independent of $L$, converts the dimensionless reference-volume rate to pressure per physical volume.

Its finite-volume partition sum, when finite, is $\Xi_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ret},0}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_0(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)$, using [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This definition sets the weight of a forbidden configuration to zero; it does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$. When $B=\varnothing$ the measure is the unrestricted Poisson activity model; for a nonempty hard core it is generally not Poisson. The convention is explicit model data and carries no statement about an arbitrary zero-width energy shell.

For a periodic cell of side $L$ in dimensionless coordinates, use the exact image energy $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Its periodic retained-admissibility weight is
$$w_{L,0}^{\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)<+\infty\}}=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{\varphi(y-x)<+\infty\text{ for every }x\in\omega,\ y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x\}}.$$
Thus every forbidden pair between distinct particles and every forbidden periodic-image pair, including a particle with one of its own nontrivial images, receives zero weight. When finite, the corresponding partition sum is $\Xi_{L}^{\mathrm{ret},0,\mathrm{per}}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_{L,0}^{\mathrm{per}}\,d\mu_{\Lambda_L,N}$. This is the periodic retained-admissibility convention; it is not an unrestricted zero-beta limit of a shell law.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Fix the selected stable regularly tempered pair model with Borel-measurable $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and activity $z>0$. For the superstable branch, require measurable even pair potentials $\varphi_s,\varphi_r$ with $\varphi=\varphi_s+\varphi_r$, where $\varphi_s$ is stable in joules and $\varphi_r(x)\geq0$ joules for every $x$. Require constants $\epsilon>0$ joules and $r_0>0$ in dimensionless coordinates such that $\varphi_r(x)\geq\epsilon$ whenever $\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\|x\|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$. These are exactly the stable-plus-nonnegative-core conditions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] for $\widehat\varphi$, after energy conversion; this is an additional model hypothesis, not a consequence of stability alone.

Under the Axiom of Choice, use the global measurable configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], consisting of locally finite simple configurations with sigma-algebra generated by bounded-Borel count maps. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$, let $T_a\omega(A)=\omega(A-a)$ be its measurable translation. A probability law $P$ on $\Omega$ is stationary exactly when $P\circ T_a^{-1}=P$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$. For a bounded Borel region $A$, equip its finite simple configuration set $\mathcal C_A$ with $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}=\sigma(N_B:B\subseteq A\text{ Borel})$, without completing it. On this space $r_A(\omega)=\omega\cap A$ is measurable: each generating count satisfies $N_B\circ r_A=N_B$, a bounded-Borel global count. Write $P_A=P\circ r_A^{-1}$ on this exact count sigma-algebra for every stationary $P$. This assertion does not extend $P_A$ to the completed quotient sigma-algebra. The reference $Q_A=Q\circ r_A^{-1}$ is the restriction of the same unit-intensity law $Q$; by [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]] and the count-generated restriction sigma-algebra, it equals the restriction to $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$ of the finite-sector law $e^{-|A|}\sum_{N\geq0}\mu_{A,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This count sigma-algebra is contained in the completed quotient sigma-algebra: in each sector, the pullback of $N_B$ is $\sum_{j=1}^N\mathbf1_B(x_j)$, a Borel function, so each count generator is quotient measurable. Thus the stated restriction of the positional measure is defined. Relative entropy and the restrictions below always use $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$, exactly as in the mathematical global supplier, rather than an unproved completion for arbitrary $P$. Indeed, a finite Borel partition of $A$ has multinomial counts under each fixed-$N$ Lebesgue sector, and summing these sector measures with the factor $e^{-|A|}$ gives independent Poisson counts of the corresponding volumes. Use the finite-region relative entropy $D(P_0\|Q_0)$ of [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]: if $P_0\ll Q_0$ and $h=dP_0/dQ_0$, then $D=\int h\log h\,dQ_0$ with $0\log0=0$; otherwise $D=+\infty$. Let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and define $\rho(P)=E_PN_C$. On stationary laws for which the finite limits exist, define
$$I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D(P_{\Lambda_L}\|Q_{\Lambda_L})}{|\Lambda_L|},\qquad \Phi(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_P[H_{\Lambda_L}^{\mathrm{free}}]}{|\Lambda_L|}.$$
For $\beta>0$, use the stationary laws with finite $I(P)$ and $\Phi(P)$ and adopt, at the selected $(\varphi,\beta,z)$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$

For the $\beta=0$ branch, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set $B=\{x:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]. A global configuration is hard-admissible when no pair of its distinct points has displacement in $B$. Restrict to stationary laws assigning probability one to hard-admissible configurations and having finite $I(P)$; adopt, at the selected $z$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$
These are two explicit parameter-specific physical model restrictions. They do not assert uniqueness for every activity or temperature, do not apply at coexistence when the minimizer set has several elements, and do not infer uniqueness from thermodynamic smoothness.

Assume AC. Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

The potential is stable if some $B\geq0$ satisfies $H_\phi(\omega)\geq-BN(\omega)$ for every finite configuration. It is superstable in the Georgii splitting convention if $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$, where $\phi_s$ is stable and $\phi_r\geq0$ everywhere and, for some $r_0,\delta>0$, $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta$ whenever $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$. It is lower regular if a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfies
$$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$
It is regular if it is lower regular and, for some $R<\infty$, $\phi(x)\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ whenever $|x|_\infty\geq R$. These are the conventions used for the interacting results on this page. A genuine divergent positive core is the separate additional condition that some nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$ and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; it is not implied by superstability.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. The far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a stationary probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. When the limit exists, write
$$\mathcal E(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}},\qquad I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
The cited results below establish existence under their stated hypotheses; this definition does not assume it for every stationary law.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. For stationary finite-intensity configuration laws, let $I(P)$ be relative entropy density with respect to the independent unit-intensity Poisson law, $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$, and $\Phi(P)$ the limiting positional energy density. The existence and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$ under these hypotheses are part of the proof below. For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$. This theorem concerns positional configurations only. If $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}$ is instead normalized against Lebesgue measure with $1/N!$, then $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$, so its logarithmic rate is $p_Q+1$.

Assume the superstable regular model and Poisson conventions of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], with stationary finite-intensity law space $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, intensity $\rho$, specific entropy $I$, and energy density $\Phi$ as there defined. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be an interval of positive length and define
$$\nu=\sup\{\rho(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ I(P)<\infty,\ \Phi(P)<\infty\},\qquad e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\Phi(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ \rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\},$$
with the supremum of an empty set equal to $0$ and the infimum of an empty set equal to $+\infty$. If $\inf D<\nu$ and $e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$, define
$$A_L=\{N_{\Lambda_L}/L^d\in D,\ H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d\leq e\}.$$
Then $A_L$ has positive Poisson probability for all sufficiently large $L$, and
$$\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Q_{\Lambda_L}(A_L) =-\min\{I(P):\rho(P)\in\overline D,\ \Phi(P)\leq e\}.$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. Define
$$\mathcal K_B=\left\{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}:P\!\left(\left\{\omega:\forall x,y\in\omega,\ x\neq y\Rightarrow x-y\notin B\right\}\right)=1\right\}.$$
For $\beta>0$ put $\mathcal M_{\beta,z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}$; at $\beta=0$ put $\mathcal M_{0,z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}$. Then there are $\beta\geq0$ and $z>0$ for which the empirical fields under the conditional law $Q_{\Lambda_L}(\cdot\mid A_L)$ and the matching periodic grand-canonical law concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of $\mathcal M_{\beta,z}$. If this minimizer set is a singleton, both empirical fields converge to it in probability in $\tau_L$. These are empirical-field conclusions. The periodically continued conditional and grand laws also converge in $\tau_L$ under the same uniqueness assumption, for all measurable local observables of at-most-linear count growth. The energy constraint is an upper event and $D$ is nondegenerate; this does not assert exact $N$, a shrinking shell, or a singular energy surface.
In the $\beta=0$ branch the finite periodic weight is explicitly $z^N$ times the indicator that no displacement between the configuration and any periodic image lies in $B$; no value is assigned to $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and let $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. For a finite configuration $\omega$, call it admissible when no pair displacement belongs to $B$; for periodic boxes require this also for every periodic image pair. Define the zero-inverse-temperature-parameter continuation (the mathematical $\beta=0$ branch) to be $z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\rm admissible}(\omega)$, explicitly retaining the hard exclusion. Then the normalized Poisson free and periodic partition rates exist and equal
$$-\min_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\},$$
where $\mathcal K_B$ is the set of stationary laws with no forbidden pair almost surely. The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in $\tau_L$. The periodically continued grand laws are relatively compact in $\tau_L$, all their accumulation points are minimizers, and if this minimizer is unique they converge to it for every measurable local observable of at-most-linear count growth. If $B=\varnothing$, this is the Poisson activity-$z$ model. For $B\ne\varnothing$, it is not an unrestricted Poisson law and does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as in [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]. Let $L\to\infty$ and let $C_L$ be probability laws on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, invariant under every translation modulo $L\mathbb Z^d$. Write $Q_L$ for unit-intensity Poisson measure and suppose
$$c_L=L^{-d}D(C_L\Vert Q_L),\qquad \sup_L c_L<\infty.$$
Let $\widetilde C_L$ be the law of the periodic continuation. Then $\widetilde C_L=E_{C_L}R_{L,\omega}$; these laws are stationary and are relatively sequentially compact in $\tau_L$ as $L\to\infty$. Their local counts are uniformly integrable. Along any convergent subsequence with limit $P$,
$$I(P)\leq\liminf_L c_L.$$
If the empirical fields $R_{L,\omega}$ converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to a fixed $P_*$, then $\widetilde C_L\to P_*$ in $\tau_L$, including expectations of every measurable local $f$ with $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ for bounded $A$. This concerns periodic continuation, not the zero extension of a configuration outside its fundamental cube.

derivations.claim: If $\beta>0$, the Borel superstable regular hypotheses are exactly those of [L0], and the physical conditional preparation agrees with the periodic Poisson-reference conditional law in [L2]: the factor $e^{-V_n}$ between $Q_{\Lambda_n}$ and the unnormalized positional measure is constant on the conditioning event and cancels in normalization. Under the stated strict inequalities, [L2] gives eventual event positivity, its rate limit, and the common-minimizer accumulation statement.

If $\beta=0$, the periodic indicator in [F2] excludes every forbidden pair, including periodic-image pairs, from the finite upper-energy event. Thus the physical event is exactly in the retained-admissibility model rather than an undefined $0\cdot(+\infty)$ expression. [L2] gives its event rate and conditional accumulation points; [L3] identifies the corresponding retained grand variational minimizers.

In either applicable branch, when the common variational minimizer set furnished by that branch is the singleton $P^\ast$ in [A2], every local-tame accumulation point of the periodically continued laws is $P^\ast$. Their local-tame relative compactness, including uniformly integrable local counts through [L4], then gives convergence of the conditioned and corresponding grand laws for each stated observable. The conclusion remains conditional on the draft mathematical results and the selected uniqueness premise.

Require the exact superstable regular hypotheses of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] for this dimensionless potential: a stable part plus a nonnegative core part bounded below by a positive constant on an $\ell^\infty$-ball, with the supplier's lower and upper regular tail conditions. Use $\widehat H=H/E_0$, $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$ for $\beta>0$, and $\widehat e=e/E_0$; then $\beta H=\widehat\beta\widehat H$. For this supplier convention, let $\nu$ be the supremum of finite-entropy, finite-energy attainable densities for $\widehat\varphi$, and write $\widehat\Phi(P)$ for the supplier's limiting positional energy density; let $e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\widehat\Phi(P):\rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\}$ be its numerical positional-energy infimum. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be a nondegenerate density interval, and require $\inf D<\nu$ and $\widehat e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$. Use the supplier's periodic cubes $\Lambda_n$ of numerical volume $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$ and define explicitly
$$A_n=\{\omega:N_{\Lambda_n}(\omega)/V_n\in D,\ H_{n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/(E_0V_n)\le\widehat e\},\qquad \widehat e=e/E_0.$$
Here $H_{n,\mathrm{per}}$ is the physical positional energy in joules in the same periodic convention; equivalently its event inequality is $H_{n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n\le e$. For every $n$ with positive event probability, the prepared law is $R_n(B)=Q_{\Lambda_n}(B\cap A_n)/Q_{\Lambda_n}(A_n)$ on the finite count sigma-algebra. Equivalently, with $M_n=\sum_{N\ge0}\mu_{\Lambda_n,N}$, $R_n(B)=M_n(B\cap A_n)/M_n(A_n)$, since $Q_{\Lambda_n}=e^{-V_n}M_n$; use the count-sigma restriction of these positional measures. This defines the density-interval/upper-energy conditional preparation and its conditioned laws. For $\beta>0$, the finite-volume grand and microcanonical weights are those of [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. For $\beta=0$, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set and use the formal retained-admissibility continuation of [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]; do not interpret $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

For both the positive-$\beta$ branch and the formal retained-hard-core $\beta=0$ branch, [[thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit]] gives eventual event positivity, the constrained entropy-rate limit, and common-minimizer accumulation points; at $\beta=0$, [[thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit]] identifies the matching retained grand law and minimizer set. If the relevant common minimizer set is the singleton adopted in [[post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniqueness]] for the multiplier pair supplied by that branch, both the conditioned laws and the corresponding periodic grand laws converge locally to $P^\ast$ for every measurable local observable $f$ with $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$ on a bounded region $A$. This is an interval-density and upper-energy result, not a fixed-particle-number or shrinking-shell theorem.

Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region in the dimensionless coordinates of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Use the completed product-Lebesgue sigma-algebra on $\Lambda^N$. For $N\geq1$, let
$$D_{\Lambda,N}=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\in\Lambda^N:x_i\ne x_j\text{ whenever }i\ne j\},\qquad \mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}=D_{\Lambda,N}/S_N,$$
where the permutation group $S_N$ acts by relabelling coordinates. Give $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ the quotient sigma-algebra: $A\subseteq\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ is measurable exactly when its preimage under the quotient map $q_N:D_{\Lambda,N}\to\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ is measurable in the trace of the completed product-Lebesgue sigma-algebra. Identify each orbit with its unordered simple configuration. For $N=0$, set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,0}=\{\varnothing\}$. If $\lambda_{\Lambda}^{\otimes N}$ is product Lebesgue measure restricted to $D_{\Lambda,N}$, define the sector reference measure by
$$\mu_{\Lambda,N}=\frac1{N!}(q_N)_\#\lambda_{\Lambda}^{\otimes N}\quad(N\geq1),\qquad \mu_{\Lambda,0}(\{\varnothing\})=1.$$
Equivalently, for every nonnegative measurable function $f$ on $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$,
$$\int f(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)=\frac1{N!}\int_{D_{\Lambda,N}}f(q_N(x_1,\ldots,x_N))\,d^{dN}x.$$
Collision diagonals have product Lebesgue measure zero, so $\mu_{\Lambda,N}(\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N})=|\Lambda|^N/N!$; in particular, symmetric integrands may use the equivalent integral over all of $\Lambda^N$. Thus $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ is a finite measure, not generally a probability. Two labelled tuples represent the same state exactly when they are in one $S_N$ orbit. The factor $1/N!$ is an adopted indistinguishable-particle positional convention, not a theorem about classical trajectories or every classical description.

Let $\mathcal C_\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{N\geq0}\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ with the disjoint-union sigma-algebra, and regard each $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ as a measure on this union supported on its $N$-point sector. Define the unit-intensity finite-region Poisson reference by
$$Q_\Lambda=e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}\mu_{\Lambda,N}.$$
Its total mass is one because $\mu_{\Lambda,N}(\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N})=|\Lambda|^N/N!$ and $e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N\geq0}|\Lambda|^N/N!=1$. This is a positional reference measure in the chosen dimensionless coordinates; it supplies no empirical claim about particle trajectories.

Let $\phi$ be stable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], fix $\beta>0$, and define $Z(L,N;\beta)$ as in that definition. For sequences $L_j\to\infty$ and integers $N_j\geq0$ with $N_j/L_j^d\to\rho$, define
$$b(\rho)=\sup\left\{\limsup_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta):\frac{N_j}{L_j^d}\to\rho\right\}.$$
Let $F$ be the concave envelope of $b$ on $[0,\infty)$, namely the supremum of $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i b(\rho_i)$ over finite lists with $\theta_i\geq0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, $\rho_i\geq0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i\rho_i=\rho$; the empty supremum is $-\infty$. On the interior of $\{\rho:F(\rho)>-\infty\}$, $F$ is finite and continuous. For every $\rho>0$ in that interior and every such sequence $(L_j,N_j)$,
$$\lim_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta)=F(\rho).$$
No claim is made at a close-packing endpoint or at any other excluded endpoint.

Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.

derivations.claim: By [A1] and [F2], the grand partition is precisely the activity sum over the canonical positional sectors used in [L2], with $\alpha=\log z$; [F1] and [L1] supply the stable-tail hypotheses and the canonical rate $F$ on its interior. In the mathematical partition, $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$ and $\widehat H=H/E_0$, so the Boltzmann factors agree.
The conditional mathematical conclusion [L2] gives both displayed Legendre–Fenchel identities, including only the stipulated closed concave endpoint extension.

Multiplication by $k_BT/\ell_0^d$ converts the dimensionless log-partition rate to physical pressure, while multiplication of the canonical rate by $-k_BT/\ell_0^d$ gives the stated positional free-energy density; the common measure normalization is fixed by [F2]. Since [L2] is a statement about thermodynamic functions, it supplies no local convergence or phase-uniqueness claim.

Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

Use $\Lambda_n=[-n-\tfrac12,n+\tfrac12)^d$, its side length $L_n=2n+1$ and dimensionless volume $V_n=L_n^d$, the periodic positional energy $H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the exact-$N$ measure $\mu_{\Lambda_n,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. Given $N_n\in\mathbb N_0$, a reduced configuration-energy center $e\in\mathbb R$ joules per dimensionless reference volume, and a width $\delta_n>0$ in the same units, define
$$S_n(N_n,e,\delta_n)=\{\omega\subset\Lambda_n:|\omega|=N_n,\ |H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n\}.$$
When $0<\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(S_n)<\infty$, the uniform positional shell law is
$$M_n(A)=\frac{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(A\cap S_n)}{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(S_n)}.$$
A shrinking energy-density shell uses some specified sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$. Its total energy width is $2\delta_nV_n$, which is $o(V_n)$ but need not be microscopic or bounded. Existence of a normalizing shell and the existence of a suitable shrinking sequence are separate theorem obligations. This is not a surface measure on an exact-energy hypersurface and not a phase-space shell for $K(p)+H_N^{\mathrm{per}}$.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Fix the selected stable regularly tempered pair model with Borel-measurable $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and activity $z>0$. For the superstable branch, require measurable even pair potentials $\varphi_s,\varphi_r$ with $\varphi=\varphi_s+\varphi_r$, where $\varphi_s$ is stable in joules and $\varphi_r(x)\geq0$ joules for every $x$. Require constants $\epsilon>0$ joules and $r_0>0$ in dimensionless coordinates such that $\varphi_r(x)\geq\epsilon$ whenever $\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\|x\|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$. These are exactly the stable-plus-nonnegative-core conditions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] for $\widehat\varphi$, after energy conversion; this is an additional model hypothesis, not a consequence of stability alone.

Under the Axiom of Choice, use the global measurable configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], consisting of locally finite simple configurations with sigma-algebra generated by bounded-Borel count maps. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$, let $T_a\omega(A)=\omega(A-a)$ be its measurable translation. A probability law $P$ on $\Omega$ is stationary exactly when $P\circ T_a^{-1}=P$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$. For a bounded Borel region $A$, equip its finite simple configuration set $\mathcal C_A$ with $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}=\sigma(N_B:B\subseteq A\text{ Borel})$, without completing it. On this space $r_A(\omega)=\omega\cap A$ is measurable: each generating count satisfies $N_B\circ r_A=N_B$, a bounded-Borel global count. Write $P_A=P\circ r_A^{-1}$ on this exact count sigma-algebra for every stationary $P$. This assertion does not extend $P_A$ to the completed quotient sigma-algebra. The reference $Q_A=Q\circ r_A^{-1}$ is the restriction of the same unit-intensity law $Q$; by [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]] and the count-generated restriction sigma-algebra, it equals the restriction to $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$ of the finite-sector law $e^{-|A|}\sum_{N\geq0}\mu_{A,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This count sigma-algebra is contained in the completed quotient sigma-algebra: in each sector, the pullback of $N_B$ is $\sum_{j=1}^N\mathbf1_B(x_j)$, a Borel function, so each count generator is quotient measurable. Thus the stated restriction of the positional measure is defined. Relative entropy and the restrictions below always use $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$, exactly as in the mathematical global supplier, rather than an unproved completion for arbitrary $P$. Indeed, a finite Borel partition of $A$ has multinomial counts under each fixed-$N$ Lebesgue sector, and summing these sector measures with the factor $e^{-|A|}$ gives independent Poisson counts of the corresponding volumes. Use the finite-region relative entropy $D(P_0\|Q_0)$ of [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]: if $P_0\ll Q_0$ and $h=dP_0/dQ_0$, then $D=\int h\log h\,dQ_0$ with $0\log0=0$; otherwise $D=+\infty$. Let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and define $\rho(P)=E_PN_C$. On stationary laws for which the finite limits exist, define
$$I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D(P_{\Lambda_L}\|Q_{\Lambda_L})}{|\Lambda_L|},\qquad \Phi(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_P[H_{\Lambda_L}^{\mathrm{free}}]}{|\Lambda_L|}.$$
For $\beta>0$, use the stationary laws with finite $I(P)$ and $\Phi(P)$ and adopt, at the selected $(\varphi,\beta,z)$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$

For the $\beta=0$ branch, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set $B=\{x:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]. A global configuration is hard-admissible when no pair of its distinct points has displacement in $B$. Restrict to stationary laws assigning probability one to hard-admissible configurations and having finite $I(P)$; adopt, at the selected $z$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$
These are two explicit parameter-specific physical model restrictions. They do not assert uniqueness for every activity or temperature, do not apply at coexistence when the minimizer set has several elements, and do not infer uniqueness from thermodynamic smoothness.

Assume AC. Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

The potential is stable if some $B\geq0$ satisfies $H_\phi(\omega)\geq-BN(\omega)$ for every finite configuration. It is superstable in the Georgii splitting convention if $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$, where $\phi_s$ is stable and $\phi_r\geq0$ everywhere and, for some $r_0,\delta>0$, $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta$ whenever $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$. It is lower regular if a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfies
$$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$
It is regular if it is lower regular and, for some $R<\infty$, $\phi(x)\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ whenever $|x|_\infty\geq R$. These are the conventions used for the interacting results on this page. A genuine divergent positive core is the separate additional condition that some nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$ and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; it is not implied by superstability.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. The far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a stationary probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. When the limit exists, write
$$\mathcal E(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}},\qquad I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
The cited results below establish existence under their stated hypotheses; this definition does not assume it for every stationary law.

Assume the superstable regular model of [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]], an interior density $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, and differentiability of $\beta\mapsto F_\beta(\rho)$ at $\beta>0$. Put $e=-\partial_\beta F_\beta(\rho)$. Suppose the grand variational minimizer at a supporting activity $z>0$ is a singleton $P_*$. Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. There exists a specified sequence $\delta_L\downarrow0$ such that the uniform positional shell law
$$Q_{\Lambda_L}\!\left(\,\cdot\ \middle|\ N=N_L,\ \left|H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d-e\right|\leq\delta_L\right)$$
is eventually defined, and its empirical field converges in probability in $\tau_L$ to $P_*$. The free and periodic exact-$N$ canonical empirical fields and the matching periodic grand-canonical empirical field converge in probability to the same limit. The energy width $2\delta_LL^d=o(L^d)$; no arbitrary prescribed width or zero-width surface measure is asserted.

Assume the superstable regular interaction of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. For integers $N_L$ with $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)$ be the $1/N_L!$-normalized positional partition on the periodized cube, with the image convention of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Then
$$L^{-d}\log Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the same rate as the free cube. Let $C^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,N_L}$ be the periodic exact-$N_L$ canonical law and $R_{L,\omega}$ its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. For any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, these empirical fields concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the minimizer set of $I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$. A singleton minimizer gives convergence in probability in $\tau_L$.

Assume the superstable regular model of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. Let $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $C_{L,N_L}$ be the free-boundary positional canonical law with exactly $N_L$ particles, and let $R_{L,\omega}$ be its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. Choose any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$ and set
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
For every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$,
$$C_{L,N_L}\{\omega:R_{L,\omega}\in U\}\longrightarrow1.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$. This is local observable equivalence for a uniformly sampled bulk location; it makes no claim about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin or about uniqueness for every interaction.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as in [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]. Let $L\to\infty$ and let $C_L$ be probability laws on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, invariant under every translation modulo $L\mathbb Z^d$. Write $Q_L$ for unit-intensity Poisson measure and suppose
$$c_L=L^{-d}D(C_L\Vert Q_L),\qquad \sup_L c_L<\infty.$$
Let $\widetilde C_L$ be the law of the periodic continuation. Then $\widetilde C_L=E_{C_L}R_{L,\omega}$; these laws are stationary and are relatively sequentially compact in $\tau_L$ as $L\to\infty$. Their local counts are uniformly integrable. Along any convergent subsequence with limit $P$,
$$I(P)\leq\liminf_L c_L.$$
If the empirical fields $R_{L,\omega}$ converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to a fixed $P_*$, then $\widetilde C_L\to P_*$ in $\tau_L$, including expectations of every measurable local $f$ with $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ for bounded $A$. This concerns periodic continuation, not the zero extension of a configuration outside its fundamental cube.

derivations.claim: The Borel superstable regular assumptions match [L0], and the hypotheses in the Statement match [L1]–[L3], including exact particle number, periodic boundary, interior density, differentiability, finite supporting $\alpha$, and singleton minimizer [A2]. [L2] fixes the periodic canonical rate. The periodic canonical conclusion uses [L1] and [L2]; the free-box result [L3] is not substituted for a periodic law. The carrier [L1] explicitly concerns positional pair energy, so [F1]–[F2] identify the physical shell with its positional shell law without adding kinetic energy; the chain rule gives $e/E_0=-\partial_{\widehat\beta}F$, and $\widehat\delta_n=\delta_n/E_0$ converts its numerical energy window to joules.

By [L1], canonical energy concentration permits construction of a sequence $\widehat\delta_n\downarrow0$ such that the shell has positive measure eventually and its uniform conditional law, the exact-$N$ canonical law, and the matching grand law have empirical fields converging in probability to $P^\ast$. Each periodic preparation is translation-invariant on its torus. Their finite-volume entropy densities are bounded: the canonical normalization, supporting activity and bounded canonical mean energy give this for the canonical law; for the shell, its entropy is the negative logarithm of its Poisson event probability, bounded using its eventually high canonical probability and the energy window; the grand pressure identity gives the grand bound. Apply [L4] to transfer all three empirical-field limits to their periodically continued laws for local tame observables. Set $\delta_n=E_0\widehat\delta_n$; therefore the physical shell widths shrink in joules per reference volume and expectations converge for each stated bounded-region observable of at-most-linear count growth.
